stories.title: Machine Investment Group Closes Second Fund at Hard Cap of $350M
stories.excerpt: Machine Investment Group, LP, a New York City-based real estate investment platform focused on opportunistic, distressed and special situations across the U.S., reached the final close of Machine Real Estate Fund II, the firm’s second flagship investment vehicle. Fund II reached its $350 million hard cap in primary commitments and has raised an additional $120 million in co-investments to date. Fund II received support from a diverse group of new and returning institutional investors, including public and private pension funds, endowments, foundations, family offices and private investors. Fund II exceeded Machine’s debut fund, Machine Real Estate Fund I, which closed in 2022 with $246 million in primary commitments and $208 million in co-investments. “We are humbled by the support of our investment partners, including both returning Fund I investors and a number of new institutional relationships, which allowed us to reach our hard cap for Fund II,” said Eric Rosenthal, co-founder and managing partner of Machine Investment Group. “Reaching our hard cap in what continues to be a challenging fundraising environment, particularly for middle market managers pursuing a diversified strategy, is a milestone we do not take for granted.” Representative Fund II investments include a special situations powered land investment in Pennsylvania, a distressed 539-unit residential property in downtown San Jose, a 229-unit senior housing property on Long Island acquired out of a distressed situation, a recently developed 1.3 million square foot industrial park in Phoenix and a strategic capital investment in a publicly traded company being repositioned as a powered land and data center development platform. The post Machine Investment Group Closes Second Fund at Hard Cap of $350M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Machine Investment Group closed Fund II at $350M hard cap, exceeding Fund I's $246M
Fund II raised additional $120M in co-investments; diverse LP base includes pensions, endowments, family offices
Strong institutional capital formation amid 'challenging fundraising environment' for middle-market diversified managers
stories.summary: Machine Investment Group, a NYC-based opportunistic/distressed CRE platform, closed its second flagship fund at $350 million in primary commitments plus $120 million in co-investments, exceeding its debut fund ($246M primary, $208M co-invest) closed in 2022. The final close attracted returning and new institutional investors including public/private pensions, endowments, foundations, and family offices. The milestone signals sustained appetite for middle-market distressed strategies despite a challenging fundraising climate.
stories.impact: Capital availability for opportunistic acquisition and repositioning remains robust for established managers with track records, reducing execution risk on value-add and distressed multifamily deals across U.S. markets. This signals confidence in near-term market dislocations (rate-driven refinance stress, overleveraged development) that will create acquisition windows for disciplined operators.

stories.title: Jamison CEO Jaime Lee Joins Kennedy Wilson as Senior Managing Director
stories.excerpt: Kennedy Wilson said Wednesday that Jaime Lee has joined the firm as senior managing director of capital markets and real estate investments. Most recently CEO of Los Angeles-based Jamison, Lee joins Kennedy Wilson as the firm continues to expand its investment management platform and deepen relationships with institutional and private capital partners. In her new role, Lee will help lead capital formation initiatives, strengthen relationships with institutional investors and strategic partners, and help drive investment opportunities across Kennedy Wilson’s global real estate platform.  “Jaime brings an exceptional combination of investment expertise, operational experience and long-standing relationships across both the private and public sectors,” said William McMorrow, chairman and CEO of Kennedy Wilson. “As we continue to grow our investment management platform and expand our capital formation capabilities, Jaime’s proven ability to build partnerships, identify opportunities and navigate complex transactions will be invaluable.” Lee joins Kennedy Wilson following more than 20 years at Jamison, where she helped transform the company into one of Southern California’s largest privately held real estate owners and developers.  The post Jamison CEO Jaime Lee Joins Kennedy Wilson as Senior Managing Director appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Jaime Lee, CEO of Jamison (20+ years), joins Kennedy Wilson as Senior Managing Director
Lee built Jamison's portfolio to ~18M SF across office, multifamily, retail, medical; major LA office-to-residential developer
Move follows Kennedy Wilson–Jamison JV announced <2 months prior targeting 4,000 units
stories.summary: Jaime Lee, who stepped down as CEO of Los Angeles-based Jamison after more than two decades, has joined Kennedy Wilson as senior managing director of capital markets and real estate investments. At Jamison, Lee grew the family firm's portfolio to approximately 18 million square feet across office, multifamily, retail, and medical properties, establishing it as one of LA's most prolific office-to-residential conversion developers. The hire bolsters Kennedy Wilson's capital formation and institutional investor relationships.
stories.impact: Lee's move to a $37B AUM global platform signals acceleration of office-to-multifamily conversion capital formation in Los Angeles and nationally. Her 20-year LA developer relationship network, combined with Kennedy Wilson's institutional capital, will unlock more conversions and mixed-use redevelopments, increasing supply of adaptive reuse product in constrained coastal submarkets and competing directly with ground-up residential development.

stories.title: Developer Iadisernia Lands Mezz Loan to Finish Hallandale, Fla., Condo Tower
stories.excerpt: More than a year after landing a $112 million loan to complete a mixed-use project in Hallandale Beach, Fla., developer Giuseppe Iadisernia has secured yet more debt. Cottonwood Group supplied a $50 million mezzanine loan for a 250-unit condo tower within the 10-acre Oasis mixed-use development at 1000 East Hallandale Beach Boulevard, about a mile west of the beach, the L.A.-based lender announced Wednesday. Construction is expected to be completed next year. Emile Schachter’s WD Capital Group brokered the debt. A representative for the lender has yet to provide figures regarding condo sales. Last year, S3 Capital had provided the $112 million construction loan for the 25-story tower, considered the last phase of the mixed-use broader development. Prices range from $580,000 and $3.5 million. Just last month, the first condo tower, also a 250-unit, 25-story high-rise, secured a temporary certificate of occupancy up to the 12th floor. The development includes a commercial portion with about 35,000 square feet of office space and 60,000 square feet of retail space, which was completed in 2024. Since the pandemic, when northerners flocked to Florida, Hallandale has been going upscale. In 2024, Witkoff and PPG Development nabbed a $273 million construction loan for a 20-story condo and hotel building within their exclusive Shell Bay golf country club. But some projects have struggled. In March, Monroe Capital sued PPG Development’s Ari Pearl and the principals of BH3 over a $70 million loan tied to Hallandale Beach Residences, The Real Deal reported. The lender alleged the developer stopped making payments in February. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Developer Iadisernia secures $50M mezzanine loan from Cottonwood Group for 250-unit condo tower, Hallandale Beach, FL
Oasis mixed-use project's final phase; first tower (250 units, 25-story) achieved partial TCO last month; completion expected 2025
Unit prices $580K–$3.5M; follows $112M construction loan from S3 Capital in 2024
stories.summary: Developer Giuseppe Iadisernia has closed a $50 million mezzanine loan from Cottonwood Group for a 250-unit condo tower within the 10-acre Oasis mixed-use development at 1000 East Hallandale Beach Boulevard in Hallandale Beach, Florida. Construction is expected to complete next year. The mezz loan supplements a $112 million construction loan provided by S3 Capital. Unit pricing ranges from $580,000 to $3.5 million; the first 250-unit tower recently achieved a temporary certificate of occupancy to the 12th floor.
stories.impact: Mezzanine lending is returning to for-sale condo development in South Florida, signaling lender confidence in pre-sales velocity and exit timing despite elevated rate environment. Developers with acceptable pre-sales and construction progress can layer mezz debt without full equity take-down, enabling faster capital recycling—relevant for multifamily projects considering condo conversion or mixed-use strategies in South Florida's supply-constrained coastal markets.

stories.title: Century 21 Redevelopment Adds Burlington, National Grocer to Tenant Roster
stories.excerpt: MCB Real Estate, an institutional commercial real estate investment management firm and developer with nationwide holdings, and Osiris Ventures, an urban retail-focused investment firm, have secured leases with two major retail brands at Century Marketplace, the $130-million mixed-use redevelopment of the 14-lot Century 21 department store assemblage at 458 86th St. in Brooklyn’s Bay Ridge neighborhood. A national grocery anchor has signed a lease at the property, becoming the first national grocer to serve the immediate Southwest Brooklyn trade area. National designer-discount retailer Burlington has also signed on, and together the two leases total 60,112 square feet. With these additions, the 120,000-square-foot Century Marketplace is now 65% pre-leased. “Century Marketplace demonstrates MCB Real Estate’s ability to execute complex structuring while delivering high quality, attractive retail to dense markets,” said MCB principal Drew Gorman. “By bringing together a nationally recognized specialty grocery anchor, and top national retailers like Burlington, we are reigniting a well-known commercial corridor and unlocking long term value for Southwest Brooklyn.” The post Century 21 Redevelopment Adds Burlington, National Grocer to Tenant Roster appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Century Marketplace (Brooklyn Bay Ridge, $130M) adds Burlington and national grocery anchor tenant; 65% pre-leased
Combined lease: 60,112 SF; grocery is first national grocer in Southwest Brooklyn trade area
MCB Real Estate and Osiris Ventures repositioning former Century 21 14-lot assemblage; total 120K SF
stories.summary: MCB Real Estate and Osiris Ventures have signed leases with Burlington (designer-discount retailer) and a national grocery anchor at Century Marketplace, a $130 million mixed-use redevelopment of the former Century 21 department store assemblage at 458 86th Street in Brooklyn's Bay Ridge. The two leases total 60,112 square feet, bringing the 120,000-square-foot property to 65% pre-leased. The grocery tenant is the first national grocer serving the immediate Southwest Brooklyn trade area.
stories.impact: Anchor grocery tenant and retail re-tenanting signals demand recovery and trade-area stabilization in Bay Ridge, potentially drawing residential absorption to nearby multifamily projects. First-time national grocer entry into this Southwest Brooklyn submarket indicates demographic density and spending power are sufficient to support experimentation by national brands, a leading indicator of residential demand and rent growth in the immediate neighborhood.

stories.title: Multi-Tenant Corona del Mar Retail Sells Above Asking Price
stories.excerpt: Coastal Commercial and Marcus & Millichap arranged the $13.7-million sale of 2515 E. Coast Highway, a prominent multi-tenant retail property located in Corona del Mar. The transaction was represented by Nathan Holthouser of Coastal Commercial and Ron Duong of Marcus & Millichap. The offering generated significant interest from the Orange County investment community, attracting more than 10 offers and multiple rounds of competitive bidding. Prospective buyers consisted primarily of high-net-worth private investors with ties to Orange County. Ultimately, the property sold for $700,000 above its asking price. “The response to this offering was exceptional, but I think sophisticated investors quickly recognized the underlying value of the real estate,” said Holthouser. “You have incredible frontage along Pacific Coast Highway, approximately 20 on-site parking spaces — which is extremely difficult to replicate in Corona del Mar — and a collection of mostly smaller commercial spaces that lend themselves well to maximizing rents over time.” The post Multi-Tenant Corona del Mar Retail Sells Above Asking Price appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Multi-tenant Corona del Mar retail, 2515 E. Coast Hwy, sells for $13.7M (+$700K above asking)
10+ offers, competitive bidding; buyers primarily high-net-worth Orange County investors
20 on-site parking spaces in parking-constrained coastal market; strong frontage on Pacific Coast Highway
stories.summary: Coastal Commercial and Marcus & Millichap facilitated the $13.7 million sale of 2515 E. Coast Highway, a multi-tenant retail property in Corona del Mar, closing $700,000 above the asking price. The offering attracted more than 10 offers and multiple rounds of competitive bidding, with buyers consisting primarily of high-net-worth private investors with Orange County ties. The property features exceptional Pacific Coast Highway frontage and approximately 20 on-site parking spaces.
stories.impact: Retail cap-rate compression in ultra-prime Orange County coastal locations reflects investor appetite for scarce, high-barrier-to-entry real estate with limited supply-growth potential. This demand for irreplaceable coastal land with parking scarcity has no direct multifamily implication but underscores that Orange County's coastal market will not see significant new supply of any product type—stabilizing retail and residential rents in the trade area.

stories.title: Walker & Dunlop Arranges Financing for Stamford Residential Conversion
stories.excerpt: Walker & Dunlop has arranged a $74.5-million loan for the acquisition and redevelopment of The Caspian, a luxury development in Stamford, CT. The Walker & Dunlop Capital Markets Institutional Advisory team led by Aaron Appel, Jonathan Schwartz, Keith Kurland, Adam Schwartz, Sean Reimer, Dustin Stolly, Jordan Casella and Stanley Cayre arranged the financing, provided by an affiliate of Apollo Global Management, on behalf of Sun Homes and Hudson Bay Capital. Located at 68-70 Seaview Ave., the project will transform an existing seven-story, 241,000-square-foot waterfront office building into 63 luxury condominium residences featuring a mix of one-, two-, and three-bedroom homes along with townhome residences. Amenities include a grand lobby, indoor and outdoor amenity spaces, private rooftop terraces, a 57-slip marina and structured parking. “Fairfield and Westchester counties remain highly supply-constrained residential markets, particularly for new waterfront product given limited developable shoreline and complex entitlement processes,” said Jonathan Schwartz. “The Caspian is uniquely positioned to address that supply-demand imbalance with a best-in-class luxury offering in one of the region’s most desirable waterfront locations. We’re grateful to Sun Homes, Hudson Bay Capital, and Apollo Global Management for their partnership in bringing this vision forward.” The post Walker & Dunlop Arranges Financing for Stamford Residential Conversion appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Walker & Dunlop arranges $74.5M construction/acquisition loan (Apollo Global) for Stamford residential conversion
The Caspian: 241K SF office building → 63 luxury condos + 57-slip marina; Fairfield/Westchester supply-constrained
Waterfront location, limited shoreline development, complex entitlements; completion timeline unstated
stories.summary: Walker & Dunlop has arranged a $74.5 million loan from an Apollo Global Management affiliate for Sun Homes and Hudson Bay Capital to acquire and redevelop The Caspian in Stamford, Connecticut. The project will convert a seven-story, 241,000-square-foot waterfront office building into 63 luxury condominiums (one-, two-, three-bedroom units and townhomes) with a 57-slip marina, indoor/outdoor amenities, rooftop terraces, and structured parking. The lender highlighted Fairfield and Westchester counties' supply constraints in luxury residential, particularly for new waterfront product.
stories.impact: Office-to-residential conversion financing is available in Fairfield/Westchester at institutional rates, signaling lender and operator confidence in conversion economics in supply-constrained suburban waterfront markets. Limited shoreline and complex entitlements create natural supply barriers; conversion economics improve as office valuations remain depressed and luxury residential premiums justify conversion capex. Developers with waterfront or near-waterfront office assets in metro NYC's suburban rings should model conversions aggressively.

stories.title: Dov Hertz Offloads Major Staten Island Industrial Site for $167M
stories.excerpt: A 53-acre industrial outdoor storage (IOS) parcel on Staten Island just changed hands for $167 million. Real estate investment firm Jadian Capital acquired the property at 1900 and 1800 South Avenue, located on the island’s west shore, from Dov Hertz’s Kadima Industrial Partners, according to broker Cushman & Wakefield. The Real Deal first reported the news. “A well-deserved congrats to Kadima Industrial Partners and our buyer for closing one of the market’s largest industrial outdoor storage trades,” Kyle Schmidt, a vice chairman at C&W, wrote in a LinkedIn post Tuesday. “Fully leased, the 53-acre property illustrates the continued user and capital demand for sites offering proximity to infrastructure and consumers.” Spokespeople for C&W, Jadian Capital and Kadima Industrial did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s requests for comment. Schmidt listed C&W brokers Gary Gabriel, Ryan Larkin, Seth Zuidema, Helen McCarthy Paul, Rico Murtha and Gurpreet Singh in his LinkedIn post as representing the seller. It is unclear who represented the buyer in this deal. Hertz’s DH Property Holdings had acquired both Staten Island sites in two separate transactions — one in 2020 and the other in 2021 — for a total of $79 million, according to TRD. Since then, the property owner spent about $10 million in capital projects on the site. The property is fully leased to asphalt mixing plant City Asphalt and auction house IAA, with both a waterfront dock and train access. Jadian will continue to operate the property as an IOS facility, according to TRD. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Jadian Capital acquires 53-acre industrial outdoor storage site (Staten Island) from Kadima Partners for $167M
1800/1900 South Avenue, west shore; fully leased; closure expected near-term
IOS parcel reflects continued capital demand for proximity to infrastructure/consumers; largest Staten Island industrial trade
stories.summary: Jadian Capital has acquired a 53-acre industrial outdoor storage (IOS) parcel on Staten Island's west shore (1800 and 1900 South Avenue) from Dov Hertz's Kadima Industrial Partners for $167 million. The property is fully leased. Cushman & Wakefield brokers noted the trade represents one of the market's largest industrial outdoor storage transactions and reflects sustained user and capital demand for sites offering proximity to infrastructure and consumers.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact; industrial-focused capital remains strong in gateway metros with constrained land and infrastructure proximity. However, a $167M industrial deal signals that development capital is not retreating despite rate uncertainty—sellers like Kadima are harvesting gains and redeploying into other assets. Market liquidity and bid-ask alignment remain reasonable for well-located trophy assets, supporting multifamily developer equity and debt financing prospects.

stories.title: Jaime Lee Joins Kennedy Wilson After Two Decades at L.A. Powerhouse Jamison
stories.excerpt: After recently stepping down as the head of her family’s real estate firm — one of the most active developers in Los Angeles — Jaime Lee is taking a new role at Kennedy Wilson as senior managing director of capital markets and investments. Kennedy Wilson has approximately $37 billion in assets under management across equity, credit and development strategies in the United States and Europe. The Beverly Hills-based investment management firm announced on Wednesday that it hired Lee. Lee will help lead capital formation, strengthen relationships with institutional investors and strategic partners, and pursue investments across the company’s global platform, the announcement said. The move follows more than two decades for Lee at Jamison, most recently as CEO, where she helped grow the family-run company’s portfolio to roughly 18 million square feet spanning office, multifamily, retail and medical properties, while establishing Jamison as one of Los Angeles’ most prolific office-to-residential developers. The move to Kennedy Wilson also comes less than two months after the firm partnered with Jamison on a major joint venture targeting 4,000 affordable units across the city, beginning with the conversion of Downtown L.A.’s former World Trade Center into 512 apartments. For her role at Jamison, Lee was regularly honored on Commercial Observer’s Power SoCal list, last year noting that Jamison had completed seven adaptive reuse projects since 2013, with three more under construction and another 10 in its pipeline at the time. At Kennedy Wilson, Lee is similarly bullish on multifamily. “As investors evaluate where to allocate capital in this next cycle, there is a particularly compelling opportunity in multifamily, where constrained supply and durable housing demand are creating attractive long-term fundamentals,” Lee said in a statement. Lee also serves on the executive committee for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic and Paralympic Games and as a California Coastal commissioner
bullets: Jaime Lee (ex-CEO Jamison, 20+ years) joins Kennedy Wilson as Senior MD, capital markets & investments
Jamison portfolio: ~18M SF office, multifamily, retail, medical; prolific LA office-to-residential converter
Kennedy Wilson: $37B AUM; hire follows Jamison JV announced <2 months ago targeting 4,000 units
stories.summary: After stepping down as CEO of Jamison, a Los Angeles family-run developer where she spent more than two decades, Jaime Lee has joined Kennedy Wilson as senior managing director of capital markets and real estate investments. At Jamison, Lee grew the firm's portfolio to approximately 18 million square feet across office, multifamily, retail, and medical assets, establishing it as one of LA's most active office-to-residential conversion developers. Kennedy Wilson manages approximately $37 billion in AUM across equity, credit, and development strategies in the U.S. and Europe.
stories.impact: Lee's transition to a $37B global platform accelerates office-to-multifamily conversion capital formation and institutional investment in urban adaptive reuse. Her 20-year LA developer network and conversion expertise, married to Kennedy Wilson's institutional capital, will unlock more projects competing with ground-up residential in supply-constrained coastal markets. This is a signal that large platforms are betting heavily on conversion economics and expect sustained conversion deal flow across major U.S. markets.

stories.title: Rexford to Sell $1.2B SoCal Portfolio to EQT
stories.excerpt: Rexford Industrial Realty is significantly slimming down its portfolio in Southern California. The Los Angeles-based industrial real estate investment trust (REIT) announced it has agreed to sell a portfolio of properties to an affiliate of EQT Real Estate for approximately $1.2 billion. The deal is expected to close by the end of the third quarter. The sale is part of Rexford’s plan to unload $1.5 billion to $2 billion in non-core properties, and improve its portfolio and balance sheet. Rexford did not disclose the properties included in the portfolio, but said more details will be provided when the transaction closes. The assets were described as having limited long-term growth potential, greater competing supply, shorter remaining lease terms or above-market rents. The portfolio sold to EQT is expected to generate a 5.5 percent cash net operating income yield in 2027 due to anticipated move-outs and the drops to what are now above-market rents. “By strategically recycling capital from select non-core assets, we are concentrating our portfolio around the properties we believe offer the strongest long-term cash flow growth and value creation opportunity,” Rexford CEO Laura Clark said in a statement. Rexford plans to use the proceeds to pay down debt maturing in 2027, potentially repurchase shares under its $1 billion buyback program, and fund its redevelopment and development pipeline. Including the EQT deal, Rexford has now closed or has under contract about $1.5 billion of dispositions this year, and is in negotiations on more properties for sale. As of June 30, Rexford owned 409 properties encompassing approximately 49.9 million rentable square feet, all concentrated in infill Southern California. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Rexford Industrial sells $1.2B SoCal portfolio to EQT Real Estate; REIT slimming down non-core assets
Part of $1.5B–$2B non-core disposition plan; assets have limited growth, above-market rents, shorter lease terms
5.5% NOI yield expected in 2027 post rent-down; closure expected Q3 2025
stories.summary: Rexford Industrial Realty has agreed to sell a portfolio of Southern California properties to an EQT Real Estate affiliate for approximately $1.2 billion, expected to close by Q3 2025. The sale is part of a larger plan to divest $1.5 billion to $2 billion in non-core assets to improve portfolio quality and balance sheet strength. The sold assets carry limited long-term growth potential, above-market rents, greater competing supply, and shorter lease terms; the portfolio is expected to generate a 5.5 percent cash NOI yield in 2027 as rents normalize downward.
stories.impact: Major REIT capital recycling in SoCal signals portfolio rebalancing away from mature, supply-competitive industrial assets toward high-growth or constrained-supply markets. This creates market testing of industrial NOI yields (5.5% NOI in 2027 on a mature, below-market-rent portfolio) and liquidity for acquirers; multifamily developers should monitor whether Rexford redeploys proceeds into residential development or partnerships in supply-constrained LA/OC submarkets, which would increase residential construction capital competition.

stories.title: Household Goods Seller Diamond Home Signs 7K-SF Lease at 20 West 36th Street
stories.excerpt: A household goods importer and distributor has signed a new office lease in Midtown South, Commercial Observer has learned. Diamond Home signed a 7,272-square-foot deal for the entire fifth floor of the Rosen family’s 20 West 36th Street with a term of ​​seven years and seven months in a relocation from 28 West 36th Street, according to the brokers. Asking rent for the building between Fifth Avenue and Avenue of the Americas was $46 per square foot, according to the landlord. Joel Kubie and Michael Beyda of Benchmark Properties negotiated on behalf of the tenant, while Max Koeppel of Koeppel Rosen, the leasing and management agent for the Rosen family portfolio, represented the landlord in-house. “This was the second deal in a short period of time that Koeppel Rosen and I have done,” Kubie said in a statement. Kubie and Beyda recently represented Expanscience, which took about 11,500 square feet at 39 West 19th Street. “Both Diamond Home and Expanscience are currently mid-renovation for their space with move-in dates in the next few months,” Kubie added. Other tenants in the 12-story property at 20 West 36th Street include security services firm Unity Building Security, which signed a lease for 3,439 square feet in November 2025, and educational development organization Publicolor, which renewed its 6,850 square feet in June 2025. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Diamond Home (household goods importer/distributor) signs 7,272 SF office lease, 20 West 36th St, Midtown South
5th floor, 7yr 7mo term, $46/SF asking rent; relocation from 28 West 36th (same block)
Second Midtown South lease by same brokers (Expanscience, 39 West 19th); both mid-renovation
stories.summary: Diamond Home, a household goods importer and distributor, has signed a 7,272-square-foot lease for the entire fifth floor of 20 West 36th Street in Midtown South, with a term of seven years and seven months at an asking rent of $46 per square foot. The tenant is relocating from 28 West 36th Street (same block). The brokers note this is the second Midtown South office lease they have negotiated in a short period, with similar tenant characteristics (both mid-renovation).
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance. Office leasing in Midtown South at $46/SF suggests modest supply-demand rebalancing in secondary Manhattan office corridors, but does not signal multifamily demand or supply shifts. Brief note: if Midtown South office recovers and tightens, nearby multifamily absorption may benefit from worker density recovery, but timing remains uncertain given persistent remote work and office oversupply.
